{"parentUuid":"9b6c3363-25d6-41cf-9e58-7dba31179c0f","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"9d985988-d062-4265-b5d1-c84da2a0fe80","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: C:\\Users\\PC\\.ccs\\instances\\nathanleewindy\\skills\\ccs-delegation\n\n# CCS Delegation\n\nDelegate deterministic tasks to cost-optimized models via CCS CLI.\n\n## Core Concept\n\nExecute tasks via alternative models using:\n- **Initial delegation**: `ccs {profile} -p \"task\"`\n- **Session continuation**: `ccs {profile}:continue -p \"follow-up\"`\n\n**Profile Selection:**\n- Auto-select from `~/.ccs/config.json` via task analysis\n- Profiles: glm (cost-optimized), kimi (long-context/reasoning), custom profiles\n- Override: `--{profile}` flag forces specific profile\n\n## User Invocation Patterns\n\nUsers trigger delegation naturally:\n- \"use ccs [task]\" - Auto-select best profile\n- \"use ccs --glm [task]\" - Force GLM profile\n- \"use ccs --kimi [task]\" - Force Kimi profile\n- \"use ccs:continue [task]\" - Continue last session\n\n**Examples:**\n- \"use ccs to fix typos in README.md\"\n- \"use ccs to analyze the entire architecture\"\n- \"use ccs --glm to add unit tests\"\n- \"use ccs:continue to commit the changes\"\n\n## Agent Response Protocol\n\n**For `/ccs [task]`:**\n\n1. **Parse override flag**\n   - Scan task for pattern: `--(\\w+)`\n   - If match: `profile = match[1]`, remove flag from task, skip to step 5\n   - If no match: continue to step 2\n\n2. **Discover profiles**\n   - Read `~/.ccs/config.json` using Read tool\n   - Extract `Object.keys(config.profiles)` → `availableProfiles[]`\n   - If file missing → Error: \"CCS not configured. Run: ccs doctor\"\n   - If empty → Error: \"No profiles in config.json\"\n\n3. **Analyze task requirements**\n   - Scan task for keywords:\n     - `/(think|analyze|reason|debug|investigate|evaluate)/i` → `needsReasoning = true`\n     - `/(architecture|entire|all files|codebase|analyze all)/i` → `needsLongContext = true`\n     - `/(typo|test|refactor|update|fix)/i` → `preferCostOptimized = true`\n\n4. **Select profile**\n   - For each profile in `availableProfiles`: classify by name pattern (see Profile Characteristic Inference table)\n   - If `needsReasoning`: filter profiles where `reasoning=true` → prefer kimi\n   - Else if `needsLongContext`: filter profiles where `context=long` → prefer kimi\n   - Else: filter profiles where `cost=low` → prefer glm\n   - `selectedProfile = filteredProfiles[0]`\n   - If `filteredProfiles.length === 0`: fallback to `glm` if exists, else first available\n   - If no profiles: Error\n\n5. **Enhance prompt**\n   - If task mentions files: gather context using Read tool\n   - Add: file paths, current implementation, expected behavior, success criteria\n   - Preserve slash commands at task start (e.g., `/cook`, `/commit`)\n\n6. **Execute delegation**\n   - Run: `ccs {selectedProfile} -p \"$enhancedPrompt\"` via Bash tool\n\n7. **Report results**\n   - Log: \"Selected {profile} (reason: {reasoning/long-context/cost-optimized})\"\n   - Report: Cost (USD), Duration (sec), Session ID, Exit code\n\n**For `/ccs:continue [follow-up]`:**\n\n1. **Detect profile**\n   - Read `~/.ccs/delegation-sessions.json` using Read tool\n   - Find most recent session (latest timestamp)\n   - Extract profile name from session data\n   - If no sessions → Error: \"No previous delegation. Use /ccs first\"\n\n2. **Parse override flag**\n   - Scan follow-up for pattern: `--(\\w+)`\n   - If match: `profile = match[1]`, remove flag from follow-up, log profile switch\n   - If no match: use detected profile from step 1\n\n3. **Enhance prompt**\n   - Review previous work (check what was accomplished)\n   - Add: previous context, incomplete tasks, validation criteria\n   - Preserve slash commands at start\n\n4. **Execute continuation**\n   - Run: `ccs {profile}:continue -p \"$enhancedPrompt\"` via Bash tool\n\n5. **Report results**\n   - Report: Profile, Session #, Incremental cost, Total cost, Duration, Exit code\n\n## Decision Framework\n\n**Delegate when:**\n- Simple refactoring, tests, typos, documentation\n- Deterministic, well-defined scope\n- No discussion/decisions needed\n\n**Keep in main when:**\n- Architecture/design decisions\n- Security-critical code\n- Complex debugging requiring investigation\n- Performance optimization\n- Breaking changes/migrations\n\n## Profile Selection Logic\n\n**Task Analysis Keywords** (scan task string with regex):\n\n| Pattern | Variable | Example |\n|---------|----------|---------|\n| `/(think\\|analyze\\|reason\\|debug\\|investigate\\|evaluate)/i` | `needsReasoning = true` | \"think about caching\" |\n| `/(architecture\\|entire\\|all files\\|codebase\\|analyze all)/i` | `needsLongContext = true` | \"analyze all files\" |\n| `/(typo\\|test\\|refactor\\|update\\|fix)/i` | `preferCostOptimized = true` | \"fix typo in README\" |\n\n**Profile Characteristic Inference** (classify by name pattern):\n\n| Profile Pattern | Cost | Context | Reasoning |\n|----------------|------|---------|-----------|\n| `/^glm/i` | low | standard | false |\n| `/^kimi/i` | medium | long | true |\n| `/^claude/i` | high | standard | false |\n| others | low | standard | false |\n\n**Selection Algorithm** (apply filters sequentially):\n\n```\nprofiles = Object.keys(config.profiles)\nclassified = profiles.map(p => ({name: p, ...inferCharacteristics(p)}))\n\nif (needsReasoning):\n  filtered = classified.filter(p => p.reasoning === true).sort(['kimi'])\nelse if (needsLongContext):\n  filtered = classified.filter(p => p.context === 'long').sort(['kimi'])\nelse:\n  filtered = classified.filter(p => p.cost === 'low').sort(['glm', ...])\n\nselected = filtered[0] || profiles.find(p => p === 'glm') || profiles[0]\nif (!selected): throw Error(\"No profiles configured\")\n\nlog(\"Selected {selected} (reason: {reasoning|long-context|cost-optimized})\")\n```\n\n**Override Logic**:\n- Parse task for `/--(\\w+)/`. If match: `profile = match[1]`, remove from task, skip selection\n\n## Example Delegation Tasks\n\n**Good candidates:**\n- \"/ccs add unit tests for UserService using Jest\"\n  → Auto-selects: glm (simple task)\n- \"/ccs analyze entire architecture in src/\"\n  → Auto-selects: kimi (long-context)\n- \"/ccs think about the best database schema design\"\n  → Auto-selects: kimi (reasoning)\n- \"/ccs --glm refactor parseConfig to use destructuring\"\n  → Forces: glm (override)\n\n**Bad candidates (keep in main):**\n- \"implement OAuth\" (too complex, needs design)\n- \"improve performance\" (requires profiling)\n- \"fix the bug\" (needs investigation)\n\n## Execution\n\n**Commands:**\n- `/ccs \"task\"` - Intelligent delegation (auto-select profile)\n- `/ccs --{profile} \"task\"` - Force specific profile\n- `/ccs:continue \"follow-up\"` - Continue last session (auto-detect profile)\n- `/ccs:continue --{profile} \"follow-up\"` - Continue with profile switch\n\n**Agent via Bash:**\n- Auto: `ccs {auto-selected} -p \"task\"`\n- Continue: `ccs {detected}:continue -p \"follow-up\"`\n\n## References\n\nTemplate: `CLAUDE.md.template` - Copy to user's CLAUDE.md for auto-delegation config\nTroubleshooting: `references/troubleshooting.md`\n"}]},"isMeta":true,"uuid":"1226510e-a184-47d0-9b78-80796bf5939b","timestamp":"2026-05-11T13:10:14.523Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"05fec586-ee41-4fa2-a25a-431e63aac372","version":"2.1.137","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"cb8c2004-1dda-4ad1-aaa6-0b4f6ea4328b","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"mcp_instructions_delta","addedNames":["plugin:context7:context7"],"addedBlocks":["## plugin:context7:context7\nUse this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service -- even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer -- your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.\n\nDo not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts."],"removedNames":[]},"type":"attachment","uuid":"d4f0e775-3771-41ab-b98e-bd9b55b66dc6","timestamp":"2026-05-11T13:10:14.522Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"05fec586-ee41-4fa2-a25a-431e63aac372","version":"2.1.137","gitBranch":"main"}
{"parentUuid":"d4f0e775-3771-41ab-b98e-bd9b55b66dc6","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- ccs-delegation: Auto-activate CCS CLI delegation for deterministic tasks. Parses user input, auto-selects optimal profile (glm/kimi/custom) from ~/.ccs/config.json, enhances prompts with context, executes via `ccs {profile} -p \"task\"` or `ccs {profile}:continue`, and reports results. Triggers on \"use ccs [task]\" patterns, typo/test/refactor keywords. Excludes complex architecture, security-critical code, performance optimization, breaking changes.\n- attach: Port the Claude Code harness layer from this project to a new project directory. Use when bootstrapping a fresh Claude Code project on the same machine, when peers want to copy the harness, or when verifying layer separation via dry-run. Reads .claude/manifest.yaml; copies harness-tagged artifacts only; excludes stockforge biz + personal layers; generates skeleton CLAUDE.md + manifest at target.\n- crawler-reliability: Build reliable web crawlers for data gathering. Use when implementing scrapers for CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz, YouTube (yt-dlp), Facebook fanpages, or any external data source. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n- ddd-tactical-patterns: Apply DDD tactical patterns (aggregate, entity, value object, repository, domain event, anti-corruption layer) correctly in Python/dataclasses code. Use when designing or implementing domain models, repositories, or cross-bounded-context communication in StockForge's 9 BCs.\n- decompose-work: Split a non-trivial task into deterministic-vs-LLM portions before execution. Use when planning multi-step work where some sub-tasks are mechanical (file ops, regex, count, schema validation) and others require judgment (synthesis, design, ambiguity resolution). Outputs structured plan that maps each portion to the cheapest competent tool. Pairs with capability-map.md (model × effort × task_class grounding) and try-n-approaches (S9 — Karpathy autoresearch loop).\n- empirical-probe-first: Probe ALL viable strategies in a multi-option ladder BEFORE committing to one. Use when a session-plan / decision-ADR / spec presents ≥3 strategy options (e.g. \"Strategy A1/A2/A3\" or \"alternative B/C/D\") and the recommended option's source-evidence may be stale. Outputs a probe matrix per strategy + commit decision with empirical citation. Pairs with `vendor-api-probe.sh` (deterministic detection layer; SessionStart hook) and `decompose-work` (deterministic-vs-LLM split per probe). Charter promotion target — codifies L-S32-1 doctrine surfaced at S32 Track A pivot (master-plan recommended A2 vnstock alternate; empirical probe rejected A1+A2; A3 SSI direct httpx adopted instead).\n- evidence-extraction: Extract structured claims from unstructured sources with citation integrity. Use when building extraction pipelines, parsing news articles or KOL transcripts, or anywhere claims are created from raw data. Ensures every claim has source_url, extracted_at, confidence, and verified attribution. Enforces no-LLM-math invariant (I-S1).\n- fastapi-module: Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions. Use when creating a new HTTP endpoint, adding routes, wiring dependency injection, configuring Pydantic DTOs. Covers router boundaries, provider patterns, testing setup. Phase 2+ only — Phase 1 uses Streamlit dashboard directly.\n- grill-maximization: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Built on the principle that human-in-the-loop time is the scarcest resource in autonomous coding.\n- hook-diagnostics: Inspect hook event lifecycle (state machine + transcript cache + aggregator output) when triaging failed/stuck hooks or auditing self-awareness rollups. Use during sandwich-verifier review, drift investigation, or post-mortem when component-telemetry.jsonl + dispatch.jsonl + sessions-rollup.tsv need cross-checking.\n- obsidian-vault: Search, create, and manage notes in the StockForge Obsidian vault with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index maintenance. Use when adding content to the knowledge base, navigating entities/concepts, or maintaining the raw/wiki separation. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed. Extended with raw/wiki pattern from Karpathy LLM Wiki.\n- postgres-pgvector: Design Postgres schemas with pgvector and TimescaleDB for StockForge. Use when creating migrations, designing tables, writing queries. Covers vector embeddings for semantic search on Vietnamese text, time-series for price/sentiment data, JSONB vs structured columns.\n- promote-rule: Cluster agent-notes.md entries by lexical similarity, propose promotion of recurring rules to deterministic hook (priority 1), skill (priority 2), or charter (priority 3). Use when agent-notes has accumulated ≥10 new rules since last promotion run, or on-demand at phase boundary. Outputs proposal markdown to observations/. Pairs with capability-map.md (writes new task_class entries) and decompose-work (consumes promotion outcomes).\n- prompt-engineering: Design and optimize LLM prompts for StockForge pipeline stages. Use when writing or refining prompts for claim extraction, KOL recommendation extraction, sentiment analysis, thesis synthesis. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Enforces no-LLM-math constraint.\n- qa-escalation: File-based Q&A protocol — composes bundle file in human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, tracks lifecycle (pending → answered → stale → processed), creates URGENT notification when needed. Use when intent classifier recommends OPEN_QA_BUNDLE / ESCALATE_HUMAN, or grill-maximization has a bundle ready to write. Pairs with grill-maximization (composes content) + Track 5 hooks (auto-move stale).\n- session-memory-l0-l1: Extract structured memories (L0 quick metadata + L1 deep) from a Claude Code session JSONL transcript. L0 is pure regex (file paths, commands, errors, failures incl. Vietnamese phrases, next step). L1 ships the prompt builder + response parser + 15+35 head/tail windowing — caller dispatches the LLM (no auto-invoke in Phase 0). Plus cleanText harness-stripper + TranscriptCache (mtime+size dual-check + LRU). Use when ingesting a session for memory promotion, computing what files/commands/failures the session touched, or preparing an offline LLM extraction.\n- spec-dual-layer: Write specifications with dual-layer structure (business narrative + agent contract). Use when authoring new specs, refining existing specs, or understanding the spec template. Ensures both human stakeholder needs and agent execution needs are served.\n- spec-to-wiki: Convert raw specifications to Obsidian wiki format with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index updates. Use when adding a new spec to the knowledge base, or when regenerating wiki view after spec changes. Maintains raw as source of truth, wiki as navigable view.\n- sync-pull: On-demand confidence-score lookup before a SCOPE+/ARCH/IMPL decision. Reads agent-workspace/memory/sync-tracker/state.tsv + weights.yaml; surfaces the relevant category's score, tier, must-grill flag, and the decision-class threshold. Output drives \"self-decide vs grill\" choice. Use whenever an agent is about to commit a non-trivial decision and needs to ground confidence in historical hit rate per Charter Principle 8 (Calibration over confidence).\n- test-pyramid-balance: Balance unit, integration, and E2E tests properly in Python/pytest. Use when deciding what test to write, reviewing test coverage, or rebalancing skewed test suite. Covers test pyramid shape, BDD vs unit tests, when to use what. Includes stock-domain-specific test categories.\n- try-n-approaches: Karpathy autoresearch outer-loop framing — given a task or signal, generate ≥3 distinct approaches (DEEPEN / BROADEN / ABANDON families), pick one per cheap-first ordering, attach a deterministic metric function (per L-S12-1), and write the experiment frame to learning-data/loop/. Use when an open question surfaces from drift / dogfood / sync-grilling and you need to commit a measurable next step. Pairs with decompose-work (deterministic-vs-LLM split per approach) + capability-map (model × effort grounding) + promote-rule (consumes outcomes).\n- ubiquitous-language: Extract a DDD-style ubiquitous language glossary from the current conversation or domain area. Use when starting work on a new bounded context, when new domain terms emerge, or when verifying consistency between business language and code. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- user-prompt-intake: Hybrid intent classifier — main session lite-detects trivial prompts, dispatches intent-classifier subagent for complex ones. Use whenever a new user prompt lands (chat or file in human-workspace/user_prompt/) and you need to route the work. Built for full-autonomous loop where every prompt must be classified before action.\n- write-a-skill: Create new Claude Code skills with proper structure, progressive disclosure, and discoverability. Use when extracting a pattern from multiple sessions into a reusable skill, or when user asks to formalize a technique. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- ccs:continue: Continue last CCS delegation session [AUTO ENHANCE]\n- ccs: Delegate task with intelligent profile selection [AUTO ENHANCE]\n- autonomous: /autonomous — Toggle Autonomous Mode (on/off/status)\n- budget-check: /budget-check — Current Session Token Budget Status\n- devils-advocate: /devils-advocate — Adversarial Critique\n- drift-check: /drift-check — Run Drift Signals DR1-DR12\n- drill-me: /drill-me — Interactive Ubiquitous Language Extraction\n- grill-me: /grill-me — Relentless Plan/Design Interview\n- handoff-read: /handoff-read — Lightweight Last Session Load\n- master-plan: /master-plan — High-Level Work Decomposition\n- session-end: /session-end — Close Work Session\n- session-start: /session-start — Begin Work Session\n- session-verify: /session-verify — Mid-Session Alignment Check\n- spec-author: /spec-author — Create Dual-Layer Specification\n- spec-to-wiki: /spec-to-wiki — Convert Raw Spec to Obsidian Wiki Format\n- ul-audit: /ul-audit — Audit Ubiquitous Language Consistency\n- vbw-check: /vbw-check — Apply Verify-Before-Write Protocol\n- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).\nTRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.\nSKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.\n- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation\n- review: Review a pull request\n- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch","skillCount":51,"isInitial":true},"type":"attachment","uuid":"4c450bea-59fa-4eb1-a6ee-7c8d94a83f3d","timestamp":"2026-05-11T13:10:14.522Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"05fec586-ee41-4fa2-a25a-431e63aac372","version":"2.1.137","gitBranch":"main"}

Use bare `VAR=value bash \"...\"` (bash native inline-env syntax).\n\n**Why:** `/usr/bin/env` on Git Bash is a Windows PE32+ binary. When Claude Code's hook executor wraps the command, the `env` prefix triggers `/usr/bin/env: /usr/bin/env: cannot execute binary file` (3 errors at SessionStart matched 3 env-prefixed hooks exactly — idle-escape-detector / phase-status-coherence / harness-health-self-scan).\n\n**How to apply:** Whenever editing `.claude/settings.json` hook entries on this Windows machine, if a hook needs an env var set, write `CLAUDE_HOOK_EVENT=SessionStart bash \"...\"` not `env CLAUDE_HOOK_EVENT=SessionStart bash \"...\"`. Verified fix 2026-05-11 — all three previously-failing hooks now exit 0.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"210a1f09-ceed-48e7-bb88-0823c686e223","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"05fec586-ee41-4fa2-a25a-431e63aac372","version":"2.1.137","gitBranch":"main"}

Read FIRST every session. | Long-lived; updated each session boundary |\n| `memory/agent-notes.md` | Learned rules from real experience (post-mortem / drift / user correction). Stale paths in CLAUDE.md or skills = anti-pattern.\n\n4. **Never edit `obsidian-vault/raw/`.** Immutable. Vault writes only to `wiki/`. {"parentUuid":"db99d30b-ac35-4ddd-b55f-ee805233a014","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"c6bb712f-68a8-4b5a-829a-01786423ee52","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01SwunUFCya8yGTWZKY5sU2x","type":"tool_result","content":"The file C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\scripts\\hooks\\idle-escape-detector.sh has been updated successfully. (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"f61cd027-1653-49a1-84a5-8eb5835e29de","timestamp":"2026-05-11T13:13:54.547Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\scripts\\hooks\\idle-escape-detector.sh","oldString":"EVENT=\"${CLAUDE_HOOK_EVENT:-UserPromptSubmit}\"","newString":"EVENT=\"${1:-${CLAUDE_HOOK_EVENT:-UserPromptSubmit}}\"","originalFile":"#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# idle-escape-detector.sh — UserPromptSubmit + SessionStart hook.\n# Detects ≥3 consecutive ROUTINE-IDLE / META-CADENCE session blocks at the top\n# (newest) of agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md and demands an escape\n# action (phase-audit subagent dispatch OR Q&A escalation) before agent slips\n# into a 4th idle session.\n#\n# Phase 3.5 / S175 deliverable. M-S171-1 prevention rule #3.\n# Pairs with phase-status-coherence.sh (same session; complementary check).\n#\n# Source-of-truth pattern markers (anchored from S148-S170 production blocks):\n#   ## S<N> — Phase <X> — ROUTINE-IDLE: ...\n#   ## S<N> — Phase <X> — META-CADENCE: ...\n# Both are zero-substantive-work session classes. ≥3 consecutive at top = the\n# 22-session stall pattern that surfaced as M-S171-1 (S148-S170, ~100K wasted main).\n#\n# Per CLAUDE.md hard rule + Phase 3.5 Hard Rule #2: every hook ships with companion\n# firing-test (scripts/hooks/firing-tests/idle-escape-detector-fire-test.sh).\n# Per UP-05 + L-S11-1: bash + POSIX tools only; no Skill tool calls.\n# Exit 0 ALWAYS (informational, not blocking).\nset -uo pipefail\ntrap 'exit 0' ERR\n\nPROJECT_DIR=\"${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}\"\nSID=\"${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID:-unknown}\"\nEVENT=\"${CLAUDE_HOOK_EVENT:-UserPromptSubmit}\"\nmkdir -p \"$PROJECT_DIR/agent-workspace/memory\" 2>/dev/null || true\n\nCE=\"$PROJECT_DIR/agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md\"\nPLANS_DIR=\"$PROJECT_DIR/agent-workspace/session-plans/pending\"\nHOOK_LOG=\"$PROJECT_DIR/agent-workspace/memory/.session-hooks.log\"\nIDLE_LOG=\"$PROJECT_DIR/agent-workspace/memory/.idle-escape.log\"\n\n# Per-hour-bucket idempotency marker per L-S108-1 (CLAUDE_SESSION_ID may be empty\n# under SessionStart on Windows → fallback to constant collides across sessions).\nBUCKET=\"$(date +%Y%m%d-%H 2>/dev/null)\"\n[ -z \"$BUCKET\" ] && BUCKET=\"unbucketed-$$\"\nMARKER=\"$PROJECT_DIR/agent-workspace/memory/.idle-escape-fired-${BUCKET}\"\nTS=\"$(date -Iseconds 2>/dev/null || date '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S')\"\n\n# Per-session 5-min cache (mirrors harness-health-self-scan.sh) to avoid re-firing\n# on every UserPromptSubmit within same session — perf budget on UserPromptSubmit\n# is <2s.\nCACHE=\"$PROJECT_DIR/agent-workspace/memory/.idle-escape-cache-${SID}\"\nif [ -f \"$CACHE\" ]; then\n  CACHE_MTIME=$(stat -c %Y \"$CACHE\" 2>/dev/null || stat -f %m \"$CACHE\" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)\n  AGE=$(( $(date +%s) - CACHE_MTIME ))\n  if [ \"$AGE\" -lt 300 ]; then\n    echo \"[$TS] idle-escape-detector: CACHE-HIT age=${AGE}s session=$SID\" >> \"$HOOK_LOG\" 2>/dev/null || true\n    exit 0\n  fi\nfi\n\n# Cleanup stale hour-bucket markers from prior buckets (L-S108-1 prevention).\nfor old_marker in \"$PROJECT_DIR/agent-workspace/memory\"/.idle-escape-fired-*; do\n  [ -f \"$old_marker\" ] || continue\n  case \"$old_marker\" in\n    *\".idle-escape-fired-${BUCKET}\") ;;\n    *) rm -f \"$old_marker\" 2>/dev/null || true ;;\n  esac\ndone\n\n# Bail gracefully if current-execution.md missing.\nif [ ! -f \"$CE\" ]; then\n  touch \"$MARKER\" 2>/dev/null || true\n  exit 0\nfi\n\nset +o pipefail\n\n# ============================================================================\n# Step 1: pull last 5 session-block ## S<N> header lines (newest-first since\n# current-execution.md prepends new sessions at top).\n# ============================================================================\nHEADERS=$(grep -m 5 -E '^## S[0-9]+[a-z]?[[:space:]]+—[[:space:]]+Phase' \"$CE\" 2>/dev/null)\nHEADER_COUNT=$(echo \"$HEADERS\" | grep -c '^## S' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)\n[[ \"$HEADER_COUNT\" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || HEADER_COUNT=0\n\nif [ \"$HEADER_COUNT\" -lt 1 ]; then\n  touch \"$MARKER\" 2>/dev/null || true\n  echo \"session=$SID ts=$TS state=NO-HEADERS detail=cannot-parse-blocks\" > \"$CACHE\" 2>/dev/null || true\n  exit 0\nfi\n\n# ============================================================================\n# Step 2: count consecutive ROUTINE-IDLE / META-CADENCE among newest blocks.\n# Stop counting at first non-idle header.\n# ============================================================================\nCONSECUTIVE=0\nLATEST_LABEL=\"\"\nLATEST_SID=\"\"\nwhile IFS= read -r line; do\n  [ -z \"$line\" ] && continue\n  if [ -z \"$LATEST_LABEL\" ]; then\n    LATEST_SID=$(echo \"$line\" | sed -E 's/^## (S[0-9]+[a-z]?).*/\\1/')\n    if echo \"$line\" | grep -qE '— ROUTINE-IDLE'; then LATEST_LABEL=\"ROUTINE-IDLE\"\n    elif echo \"$line\" | grep -qE '— META-CADENCE'; then LATEST_LABEL=\"META-CADENCE\"\n    else LATEST_LABEL=\"ACTIVE\"\n    fi\n  fi\n  if echo \"$line\" | grep -qE '— (ROUTINE-IDLE|META-CADENCE)'; then\n    CONSECUTIVE=$((CONSECUTIVE + 1))\n  else\n    break\n  fi\ndone <<< \"$HEADERS\"\n\n# ============================================================================\n# Step 3: scan session-plans/pending/ for queued plans (informational boost —\n# idle while plans are queued = stronger escape signal).\n# ============================================================================\nPENDING_PLANS=0\nif [ -d \"$PLANS_DIR\" ]; then\n  PENDING_PLANS=$(find \"$PLANS_DIR\" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.md' -type f 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]')\n  [[ \"$PENDING_PLANS\" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || PENDING_PLANS=0\nfi\n\n# ============================================================================\n# Step 4: severity classification.\n#   - GREEN: 0-2 consecutive idle\n#   - YELLOW: ≥3 consecutive idle, no pending plans\n#   - RED: ≥3 consecutive idle AND pending plans ≥1 (work queued + ignored)\n# Threshold ≥3 anchors to L-S171-1 / M-S171-1 doctrine.\n# ============================================================================\nSTATE=\"GREEN\"\nSEVERITY=\"LOW\"\nif [ \"$CONSECUTIVE\" -ge 3 ] && [ \"$PENDING_PLANS\" -ge 1 ]; then\n  STATE=\"RED\"\n  SEVERITY=\"HIGH\"\nelif [ \"$CONSECUTIVE\" -ge 3 ]; then\n  STATE=\"YELLOW\"\n  SEVERITY=\"MEDIUM\"\nfi\n\n# Cache the result regardless (so cache-hit fast-path holds for next 5 min).\n{\n  printf 'session=%s ts=%s state=%s severity=%s consecutive=%d latest_sid=%s latest_label=%s pending_plans=%d\\n' \\\n    \"$SID\" \"$TS\" \"$STATE\" \"$SEVERITY\" \"$CONSECUTIVE\" \"$LATEST_SID\" \"$LATEST_LABEL\" \"$PENDING_PLANS\"\n} > \"$CACHE\" 2>/dev/null || true\n\n# Always log a one-line summary for telemetry (passive observability).\necho \"[$TS] idle-escape-detector: state=$STATE consecutive=$CONSECUTIVE latest=$LATEST_SID(${LATEST_LABEL}) pending_plans=$PENDING_PLANS session=$SID\" \\\n  >> \"$HOOK_LOG\" 2>/dev/null || true\n\n# Idempotent fire: if marker already touched this hour-bucket, suppress system-reminder\n# emission BUT keep cache + log fresh (so observability doesn't go silent).\nif [ -f \"$MARKER\" ]; then\n  exit 0\nfi\n\n# ============================================================================\n# Step 5: emit signal on RED/YELLOW.\n# ============================================================================\nif [ \"$STATE\" = \"GREEN\" ]; then\n  touch \"$MARKER\" 2>/dev/null || true\n  exit 0\nfi\n\n# Audit log entry capturing escape trigger (richer than .session-hooks.log).\n{\n  printf '[%s] %s state=%s consecutive=%d latest=%s(%s) pending_plans=%d session=%s event=%s\\n' \\\n    \"$TS\" \"ESCAPE-TRIGGER\" \"$STATE\" \"$CONSECUTIVE\" \"$LATEST_SID\" \"$LATEST_LABEL\" \"$PENDING_PLANS\" \"$SID\" \"$EVENT\"\n} >> \"$IDLE_LOG\" 2>/dev/null || true\n\nREMINDER_BODY=\"IDLE-ESCAPE-DETECTOR: state=$STATE (consecutive_idle=$CONSECUTIVE; Use bare `VAR=value bash \"...\"` (bash native inline-env syntax).\n\n**Why:** `/usr/bin/env` on Git Bash is a Windows PE32+ binary. When Claude Code's hook executor wraps the command, the `env` prefix triggers `/usr/bin/env: /usr/bin/env: cannot execute binary file` (3 errors at SessionStart matched 3 env-prefixed hooks exactly — idle-escape-detector / phase-status-coherence / harness-health-self-scan).\n\n**How to apply:** Whenever editing `.claude/settings.json` hook entries on this Windows machine, if a hook needs an env var set, write `CLAUDE_HOOK_EVENT=SessionStart bash \"...\"` not `env CLAUDE_HOOK_EVENT=SessionStart bash \"...\"`. Verified fix 2026-05-11 — all three previously-failing hooks now exit 0.","new_string":"---\nname: Windows hook env-var passing gotcha\ndescription: On Windows Git Bash, neither `env VAR=val bash ...` nor bare `VAR=val bash ...` prefix forms are reliable in .claude/settings.json hook commands — pass the value as a positional arg instead\ntype: feedback\n---\n\nIn `.claude/settings.json` hook commands on Windows + Git Bash, do NOT use inline-env prefix at all. Pass the event/variable as a **positional argument** to the script and have the script consume `$1` with fallback to env var.\n\n**Why:** Two failure modes ping-pong on Windows depending on spawn topology:\n- Bare form `VAR=val bash \"script.sh\"` → `bash: VAR: No such file or directory` (Claude Code's outer wrapper passes the inline-env-arg through to a layer that doesn't recognize it)\n- Env-prefixed form `env VAR=val bash \"script.sh\"` → `/usr/bin/env: /usr/bin/env: cannot execute binary file` (PE32+ env binary breaks the wrapper)\n\nBoth observed in same project (S245 checkpoint + 2026-05-11 session). Local bash invocation works for either form, so testing in main bash doesn't reproduce — only Claude Code's hook executor on Windows fails.\n\n**How to apply:** When a hook needs a per-event variable (e.g. `CLAUDE_HOOK_EVENT`), write hook command as `bash \"${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}/scripts/hooks/foo.sh\" SessionStart` and in the script use `EVENT=\"${1:-${CLAUDE_HOOK_EVENT:-default}}\"`. No inline-env in settings.json — ever. Local smoke tests didn't reproduce. The firing-test fixture exercises bash invocation but NOT Claude Code's actual hook-spawn path → AP-23 class.\n\n## Fix applied\n\n### settings.json (6 hook commands reformatted)\n\nBefore:\n```json\n\"command\": \"env CLAUDE_HOOK_EVENT=SessionStart bash \\\"${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}/scripts/hooks/idle-escape-detector.sh\\\"\"\n```\n\nAfter:\n```json\n\"command\": \"bash \\\"${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}/scripts/hooks/idle-escape-detector.sh\\\" SessionStart\"\n```\n\nLines affected: 204, 208, 212 (SessionStart variants) + 277, 281, 285 (UserPromptSubmit variants).\n\n### Hook scripts (3 files, 1-line change each)\n\nBefore: `EVENT=\"${CLAUDE_HOOK_EVENT:-default}\"`\nAfter:  `EVENT=\"${1:-${CLAUDE_HOOK_EVENT:-default}}\"`\n\n- `scripts/hooks/idle-escape-detector.sh:26` (default UserPromptSubmit)\n- `scripts/hooks/phase-status-coherence.sh:30` (default UserPromptSubmit)\n- `scripts/hooks/harness-health-self-scan.sh:288` (default unknown)\n\nBackward compatibility: env-var fallback preserved, so if some caller still uses `CLAUDE_HOOK_EVENT=X bash script.sh` form (or direct test invocation with no $1), it still works.\n\n## Verification\n\n```\nbash scripts/hooks/idle-escape-detector.sh SessionStart       → exit 0\nbash scripts/hooks/phase-status-coherence.sh SessionStart      → exit 0\nbash scripts/hooks/harness-health-self-scan.sh SessionStart    → exit 0\nbash scripts/hooks/idle-escape-detector.sh UserPromptSubmit    → exit 0\nbash scripts/hooks/phase-status-coherence.sh UserPromptSubmit  → exit 0\nbash scripts/hooks/harness-health-self-scan.sh UserPromptSubmit → exit 0\npython -c \"import json;
